lockFileMaintenance.description: Never automerge. A lockfile refresh crosses a major boundary for any dependency whose manifest range has no upper bound, and it does so without raising a major-version PR to review. That is precisely how mcp 2.0.0 reached nous main on 2026-08-10 and broke it. automerge is false by default here, but it is stated explicitly so a future edit has to argue with this comment.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass both the Monday branch-creation window and the release-age quarantine below, so a CVE fix is not held for up to a week. Whether one merges unattended is still decided by the update-type rules below, so a security major keeps its human review.

packageRules.description: Automerge low-risk updates once required checks pass. The release-age quarantine is what makes unattended merging defensible: it is the window in which a broken or compromised release is normally yanked. config:best-practices ships this for npm only (security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm), so it is set here to cover every other ecosystem in the fleet (PyPI, Docker, GitHub Actions, Terraform, Galaxy, pre-commit). Note it stacks with schedule:weekly: a release cut on a Saturday is not 3 days old on Monday and waits for the following window. Lower this to '1 day' if that latency is not wanted.

Group all GitHub Actions updates so concurrent bumps do not collide on the same workflow files. separateMajorMinor is on by default, so majors still split into their own 'github-actions (major)' PR, which the major rule below labels and keeps out of automerge.
Group non-major Python dependency updates into a single PR.

Major updates: separate, labelled, never automerged, across every manager. Majors already fail to match the automerge rule above, so automerge is false by default; it is stated for the same reason as lockFileMaintenance. This rule deliberately carries no matchManagers so that a major GitHub Actions, Docker, or Terraform bump is labelled for review like a major code dependency.
